R86 found the axis that predicts benefit is COMPLEMENTARITY: on all four eICU pools, in every adequacy quartile, targets gain more from partners whose schemas overlap them LESS, orthogonal to adequacy (rho with EPV -0.036, with n -0.024). PREDICTION: schema_complement beats random on mean benefit on eICU by more than size_largest does, i.e. it clears the Result 17 ceiling that was measured on the wrong axis. FALSIFIABLE AND CHEAP: if schema_complement is no better than random, then R86 describes which decisions are good without being a lever for making them better, and the complementarity-weighted estimator in HYPERGRAPH-COMPLEMENTARITY-PLAN.md is not worth writing -- that is the kill condition C1 and it is deliberately first. CONTROL: schema_similar is run as the mirror. If BOTH beat random by the same margin then the effect is 'selecting on schema at all' rather than complementarity, which would be a different and much weaker claim. On mimic4_sites the R86 gradient REVERSES (care units inside one hospital, not separate institutions), so schema_complement should be no better or worse there -- that is the negative control that distinguishes a real mechanism from a fitting artefact.
